messages:
Morgan Lee: Heads up — around 06:12 UTC we saw sustained 5xx from inference-gateway in eu-west-1 and GPU pod churn on the thin-pool. Started routing to ams and sfo, but noticed higher tail latency on long-seq jobs.
Priya Patel: saw the same, graph shows egress retransmits spiking from the cloud provider side ~06:08. network team alerted provider.
Javier Gomez: confirmed GPU pods OOM/killed while node network flapping. Pods recovered but KV cache warming failed for a subset of requests.
Ellie Chen: redirected 25% traffic to ams, then another 25% to sfo — partial relief but not full; cost for sfo burst is higher.
Zach W.: @Morgan can you share the shift command you ran? we should capture exact steps for runbook.
Morgan Lee: ran `./ops/traffic-shift --from eu-west-1 --to ams,sfo --percent 50 --grace 120s` (history in deploy-bot). kept routing policy set to latency-first.
deploy-bot: Traffic-shift executed by Morgan Lee at 2026-03-12T06:16:14Z — from eu-west-1 -> [ams,sfo] 50% 
Priya Patel: provider says egress fabric was congested in eu-west-1 for 10-12 minutes and their mitigation created transient route churn.
Javier Gomez: root cause looks like provider-level egress congestion + our thin-pool node eviction sensitivity. we need both detection and automated mitigation.
Ellie Chen: immediate wins: 1) add egress-congestion detection alert (RTT + retransmit threshold), 2) tweak thin-pool eviction backoff for network-related terminations.
Zach W.: agree. also add a pre-check in traffic-shift to ensure KV-cache warm pool is at X% before moving >30% traffic. saved us some errors.
Morgan Lee: action items I can take now: open PR to ops runbook, add detection alert, and a small script to check warm-pool health. will also add cost estimate note for sfo burst.
Priya Patel: please add automated fallback rule: if 5xx rate > 2% for 2m and provider-retransmits > 1000 then start incremental reroute with 30s cadence.
Javier Gomez: I'll prepare a patch to thin-pool eviction logic to ignore node KILLs with network-reason for 3m. test in staging tomorrow.
Ellie Chen: Opt-in config for dedicated customers to prefer region affinity vs cost should be documented too. product wants a note. 
Morgan Lee: logging: capture `netstat -s` style retransmit counters and attach to incident bundle. also include provider ticket id.
Zach W.: I'll draft the runbook edit and PR: https://git.company/redwood/infrastructure/merge_requests/5982 — will tag for review.
Priya Patel: scheduling: assign follow-ups — monitoring alert by Priya, runbook PR by Zach, thin-pool patch by Javier, warm-pool script by Morgan.
Morgan Lee: @ops-bot please create GitHub issues from this thread and link MR. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Created issues #8213 (egress-alert), #8214 (warm-pool-check), #8215 (thin-pool-eviction-tune) and linked MR 5982.
Ellie Chen: Estimate on cost delta for the shift: roughly +12% for that hour due to sfo burst — we should include in post-incident cost recap.
Javier Gomez: test plan for patch: simulate synthetic retransmit spike in staging, verify eviction suppressed and KV-cache warm persists.
Zach W.: Will merge runbook PR after 1 reviewer and add a short checklist: detection -> verify warm pool -> run incremental shift -> monitor cost/latency -> rollback condition.
Morgan Lee: final note: replace ambiguous "failover" wording in older docs with explicit "egress-congestion reroute" and include provider escalation checklist. 
Priya Patel: Thanks all — great collaboration. I'll close the incident after the follow-ups are assigned and MR merged. :heavy_check_mark:
